name: Pilomatrixoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Pilomatrixoma

criteria.description: Firm, solitary, painless subcutaneous nodule typically located on head, neck, or upper extremities
Presence of basaloid cells and shadow (ghost) cells with calcification on biopsy
Ultrasound showing well-defined hypoechoic mass with internal calcifications

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical presentation plus confirmatory histopathological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires histopathological confirmation; imaging supports but is not diagnostic.

imaging: Ultrasound: well-circumscribed hypoechoic mass with internal calcifications
CT/MRI (rarely used): lesion with calcifications and soft tissue density
other: Histopathology: basaloid cells, shadow (ghost) cells, calcification, and sometimes ossification

distinguishingFeatures: Histology shows keratin-filled cyst lined by squamous epithelium
Dimple sign positive on lateral compression
Ulcerated or pearly lesion with telangiectasia
Histology shows basaloid tumor cells with peripheral palisading

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of lesion
Regional lymphadenopathy or signs of metastasis
references: Lever's Histopathology of the Skin, 11th Edition, 2014
